Content: Cancer research involves the investigation of many cell factors. `text(One)` factor is the stage of the cell cycle the cancer cells are in. A scientist conducted an investigation using various forms of cancer cells to compare the `text(percentage)` of cells that are in `text(each stage)` of the cell cycle. The graph below shows a summary of the data from `text(one)` study.
problems/FL26HSB/media/1a.jpg
Which analysis of these data can be made?

A.Choice: The cancer cells spend less time in the `text(G)_2` stage than the control cells do.

B.Choice: There is a greater `text(percentage)` of Cancer `text(Y)` cells than Cancer `text(X)` cells in the `text(M)` stage.

C.Choice: There is a lower `text(percentage)` of any type of cancer cells than the control cells in the `text(G)_1` stage.

D.Choice: The control and Cancer `text(Y)` cells spend more time in the `text(S)` stage than Cancer `text(X)` and Cancer `text(Z)` cells do.

Content: The process of meiosis is `text(one)` way the cells of organisms prepare to divide. Which of the following is a characteristic of meiosis that results in genetic variation?

A.Choice: division of somatic cells

B.Choice: formation of spindle fibers

C.Choice: replication of genetic material

D.Choice: crossing over of chromosomes

Content: In `1995`, scientists transferred a gene from wild rice into a type of cultivated rice. The expression of the transferred gene resulted in the cultivated rice being resistant to a specific bacterium that causes a deadly disease in rice plants. Which of the following `bbtext(best)` describes a benefit to society of this example of biotechnology?

A.Choice: a reduction in the amount of nutrients removed from rice fields

B.Choice: a reduction in the need to apply fertilizers to rice fields

C.Choice: an increase in tolerance of rice for drought conditions

D.Choice: an increase in the production of rice for food

Content: `text(Three)` varieties of mangroves are found along the coastal regions of Florida. The red and the white mangroves inhabit the eastern and western coastal areas as far north as `29°` latitude. The black mangrove overlaps with the other `text(two)` varieties and grows even farther north, up to `30°` latitude. Which of the following factors `bbtext(most likely)` contributes to the more northern aquatic range of the black mangrove?

A.Choice: The black mangrove survives in colder water temperatures.

B.Choice: The black mangrove prefers the shallower coastal waters in the north.

C.Choice: The Gulf Stream provides nutrient-rich waters for the black mangrove.

D.Choice: The more northern waters provide the black mangrove with proper salinity levels.

Content: A patient visits a physician because of a sore throat. The physician diagnoses the patient with an infection and determines that antibiotics will not be effective. Which of these is the `bbtext(most likely)` cause of this infection?

A.Choice: bacteria

B.Choice: fungi

C.Choice: protozoans

D.Choice: viruses

Content: In `text(December of 1952)`, the amount of smoke and sulfur dioxide in the air of London, England, dramatically increased. A thick layer of smog covered the city as a result of a lack of wind and of an increase in burning coal to provide heat. The table below shows some of the data collected during the `text(first half)` of the `text(month)`.
:table:problems/FL26HSB/supps/FL26HSB-T1.json
Which statement `bbtext(best)` describes the potential long-term effects on people who live in locations where these types of environmental conditions occur consistently throughout the `text(year)`?

A.Choice: Sulfur dioxide and smoke levels that rise quickly result in more respiratory illnesses than if the levels rise slowly.

B.Choice: Repeated exposure to greater levels of smoke and sulfur dioxide may lead to an increased risk of respiratory problems.

C.Choice: The elevation of sulfur dioxide levels occurs when smoke levels are also high, leading to illnesses in younger individuals.

D.Choice: The most harmful level of pollutants affecting human health occurs when the amount of smoke and sulfur dioxide reach the same level.

Content: In the `text(1830s)`, Matthias Schleiden examined the structure of plant cells and Theodor Schwann examined the structure of animal cells. After discussing their findings, they proposed an early version of the cell theory. Which of the following statements `bbtext(best)` describes why developing the cell theory was a scientific process?

A.Choice: They created a hypothesis that was believed by other scientists.

B.Choice: They provided procedures that were approved by other scientists.

C.Choice: They made observations that could be repeated by other scientists.

D.Choice: They formed a conclusion that was immediately accepted by other scientists.

Content: Students are asked to classify an unknown organism into the appropriate kingdom. The organism is multicellular with eukaryotic cells arranged into tissues. The cells of the organism do not have cell walls, and the organism is heterotrophic. In which of the following kingdoms should this organism `bbtext(most likely)` be placed?

A.Choice: Animalia

B.Choice: Fungi

C.Choice: Plantae

D.Choice: Protista

Content: Students are investigating the types of fish that live at different ocean depths. Which of the following describes characteristics of a fish that is `text(best)` suited to live in deep ocean environments?

A.Choice: a fish that is blue on the top and white on the bottom to reduce predation from above and below

B.Choice: a dark-colored fish that is adapted to cold water and uses a chemical light source to attract food

C.Choice: a blue-colored fish that feeds heavily on the types of algae that could damage a coral-reef system

D.Choice: a fish that relies on low-light conditions, on water with a high oxygen level, and on the use of a gas-filled chamber

Content: A student read an article about the positive effects of extended exercise on the cardiovascular system. The student designed the investigation described below to test the claim that exercise decreased a person’s blood pressure.

:ibox:`1`. Record the initial blood pressure of `12` participants at `text(noon)` on `text(day 1)` of the investigation.

`2`. On `text(day 1)`, `text(each participant)` exercises for `text(30 minutes)` by either walking on a treadmill or riding an exercise bicycle.

`3`. `text(Each participant)` alternates the type of exercise performed for `text(30 minutes)` for `text(six)` consecutive `text(days)`, followed by `text(one day)` of rest, for `text(12 weeks)`.

`4`. At `text(noon)` on the `text(seventh day)` of `text(each week)`, record the blood pressure of `text(each participant)`.

`5`. At the end of `text(12 weeks)`, calculate the change in blood pressure for `text(each participant)` and calculate the average change in blood pressure for the group.
Which of the following would most improve the design of the student’s investigation?

A.Choice: Include participants that do not exercise for comparison.

B.Choice: Have `text(each participant)` conduct a different type of exercise.

C.Choice: Allow some participants to exercise for longer periods of time.

D.Choice: Measure blood pressure of the participants during exercise `text(each day)`.

Content: Despite the results of this investigation, community members are concerned that the continued use of these compounds will have a negative impact on the river ecosystem. Which of the following actions will `bbtext(best)` provide a long-term solution to sustaining the life in the river?

A.Choice: Add more fish to the river.

B.Choice: Decrease the growth of algae in the river.

C.Choice: Add more plants between the golf course and the river.

D.Choice: Increase the downward slope from the golf course toward the river.

Content: The olfactory bulb is the structure in the brain that is responsible for the sense of smell. Scientists used fossils of extinct dinosaurs and prehistoric birds to estimate the size of their olfactory bulbs and their bodies. The graph below shows their data.
problems/FL26HSB/media/16a.jpg
Which of the following is the `bbtext(best)` inference from these data?

A.Choice: Smaller organisms may have detected different kinds of odors than larger organisms did.

B.Choice: Larger organisms detected odors with stronger scents compared with other types of organisms.

C.Choice: The largest of these organisms may have been able to detect more odors than the smallest of these organisms did.

D.Choice: Organisms of moderate sizes have the least range of ability to detect odors when compared with smaller and larger organisms.

Content: Cellular metabolism requires constant transfers of energy throughout the cell. Which of the following statements explains how energy is released for cellular use?

A.Choice: Cells release the `text(three)` phosphates attached to ADP `text(one)` at a time to provide energy.

B.Choice: The removal of a phosphate from ATP releases energy for metabolic activity.

C.Choice: Cellular energy is released when additional phosphates are bonded to ATP.

D.Choice: Energy is released as ADP, and a phosphate is broken down into ATP.

Content: Chickens of a certain breed have either black feathers (`text(C)^text(B)text(C)^text(B)`), white feathers (`text(C)^text(W)text(C)^text(W)`), or blue-gray feathers (`text(C)^text(B)text(C)^text(W)`). When `text(two)` chickens of this breed are crossed, they produce offspring that either have white feathers or blue-gray feathers. Which of the following parental genotypes would produce offspring with these phenotypes?

Content: When a population dramatically declines in size, the amount of genetic variation in the population also declines. Often, the population size then increases, but the amount of genetic variation does not immediately increase, as shown in the graph below.
problems/FL26HSB/media/19a.jpg
problems/FL26HSB/media/19b.jpg
Which of the following would `text(most)` contribute to the increase in the amount of genetic variation that begins at point `text(X)`?

A.Choice: The amount of gene flow between populations of different organisms decreases.

B.Choice: The number of chromosomes in gametes of the remaining organisms increases.

C.Choice: The amount of random mating within the population of organisms decreases.

D.Choice: The number of DNA mutations that are beneficial to the organisms increases.

Content: Vacuoles are membrane-bound sacs found within the cytoplasm of both plant and animal cells. Which of the following `bbtext(best)` describes how the vacuoles in plant cells differ from the vacuoles in animal cells?

A.Choice: Vacuoles in plant cells are larger than vacuoles in animal cells because they contain greater amounts of water that help support the cells.

B.Choice: Vacuoles in plant cells are larger than vacuoles in animal cells because they contain pigments that are vital to the process of photosynthesis.

C.Choice: Vacuoles in plant cells are smaller and more numerous than vacuoles in animal cells because they contain molecules that fight oﬀ foreign invaders.

D.Choice: Vacuoles in plant cells are smaller and stacked closer together than vacuoles in animal cells because they have proteins that transport materials throughout the cells.

Content: The heat of lava from an erupting volcano melts the remaining snow and ice on its slopes. This results in massive flows of mud and water that erode riverbanks and remove many plant species near the riverbanks. Which of the following is the `bbtext(most likely)` immediate consequence of this type of local loss of biodiversity?

A.Choice: The rate of nutrient recycling would increase along riverbanks.

B.Choice: `text(Secondary)` consumers would begin to move into areas near riverbanks.

C.Choice: Herbivores that feed along riverbanks would need to find food in other places.

D.Choice: The amount of energy available to consumers along riverbanks would increase.

Content: The illustration below shows the structure of the rough endoplasmic reticulum.
problems/FL26HSB/media/22a.jpg
Which statement describes how the structure of the rough endoplasmic reticulum aids overall cell function?

A.Choice: The wide layers provide a site for the synthesis of spindle fibers.

B.Choice: The multiple folds provide ample surface area for protein synthesis.

C.Choice: The irregular shape allows for the engulfing of waste products for excretion.

D.Choice: The interconnecting membrane allows for the transport of DNA to other cell organelles.

Content: The graph below represents the growth of `text(two)` different populations of a grazing vertebrate herbivore species. These populations inhabit `text(two)` different ecosystems that are of similar size.

Which of the following statements best relates the carrying capacity of `text(each ecosystem)` to the long-term growth patterns of these `text(two)` populations?

A.Choice: Competition for access to water is less in the ecosystem of population `text(Y)`, resulting in a lower carrying capacity than the ecosystem of population `text(X)`.

B.Choice: The ecosystem of population `text(Y)` contains fewer predators that consume less prey than the ecosystem of population `text(X)`, resulting in a lower carrying capacity.

C.Choice: Additional members of the species are more able to migrate into the ecosystem of population `text(X)`, resulting in a greater carrying capacity than the ecosystem of population `text(Y)`.

D.Choice: The ecosystem of population `text(X)` receives more rain that produces greater amounts of plant growth than the ecosystem of population `text(Y)`, resulting in a greater carrying capacity.

Content: Animals feed on plants that contain starch, which is broken down into glucose. Which of the following is the primary function glucose serves in an animal’s body?

A.Choice: facilitating cellular transport

B.Choice: providing a source of energy

C.Choice: regulating chemical reactions

D.Choice: transmitting signals between cells

Content: Rochelle observes a slide of an onion root tip through a microscope. She wants to identify the number of cells in `text(each phase)` of mitosis. Which of the following does Rochelle observe in the cells that are in metaphase?

A.Choice: chromosomes that are at opposite poles of the cell

B.Choice: chromosomes that are aligned in the middle of the cell

C.Choice: chromosomes that are surrounded by the nuclear membrane of the cell

D.Choice: chromosomes that are located between the equator and the poles of the cell

Content: Early scientists observed that flies developed from food sources. They formed the idea that organisms can grow from nonliving matter. Later scientists showed that organisms did not grow in sterilized food that was covered, but they did grow if the sterilized food was uncovered. These scientists formed the idea that living organisms can only be reproduced from other living organisms. Which of the following `bbtext(best)` describes why the work of these later scientists meets the criteria to be considered science?

A.Choice: The later scientists controlled the variables of an experiment instead of relying on observations.

B.Choice: The later scientists were trained in how to make an observation instead of how to form a hypothesis.

C.Choice: The later scientists based their conclusion on logic and reasoning instead of gathering additional evidence.

D.Choice: The later scientists presented a specific set of evidence instead of forming a valid conclusion for a wide range of situations.

Gene mutations may cause changes to phenotypes. Such mutations can be inherited. Which of the following must occur for a gene mutation to cause a phenotypic change that is passed on to the next generation?

A.Choice: The mutation must be caused by radiation.

B.Choice: The mutation must affect the DNA of a gamete.

C.Choice: The mutation must affect the DNA of a somatic cell.

D.Choice: The mutation must be caused by a random replication error.

Content: At specific times in the cell cycle, cells contain chromosomes with sister chromatids. Mistakes sometimes happen during the cell cycle, and the sister chromatids do not separate from each other. Which of the following `text(best)` explains how an improper separation of sister chromatids can lead to phenotypic changes in an organism?

A.Choice: The chromosomes in daughter cells have unequal numbers of mutations.

B.Choice: The chromosomes in daughter cells do not contain centromeres.

C.Choice: Daughter cells cannot use the chromosomes during replication.

D.Choice: Daughter cells contain different numbers of chromosomes.

Content: Scientists have determined that approximately `text(20 percent)` of the blood in the human body flows to muscles when at rest. Which of the following `bbtext(best)` explains how blood flow is expected to change during exercise?

A.Choice: Exercise increases the heart rate, which causes more blood to flow to the muscles.

B.Choice: Exercise increases blood pressure, which decreases the rate of blood flow to the muscles.

Content: A student compared the structures of plant cells and animal cells. After creating a list of similarities and differences between the cells, the student wrote the sentence below.
:box:Animal cells have mitochondria, but plant cells do not.
Which statement `bbtext(best)` evaluates this claim?

A.Choice: Correct — animal cells have mitochondria, and plant cells do not need to break down glucose.

B.Choice: Correct — animal cells have mitochondria, and plant cells use chloroplasts to break down glucose.

C.Choice: Incorrect — plant cells and animal cells have mitochondria because both cell types need to break down glucose.

D.Choice: Incorrect — plant cells have mitochondria and animal cells do not because animal cells do not need to break down glucose.

Content: Cooking eggs denatures the structure of the protein in egg whites. When the protein is denatured, the egg white changes appearance from clear to white. A student investigated how cooking egg whites on a stove and cooking egg whites in a microwave affected the amount of protein that was denatured. The student used an instrument to measure the `text(percent)` of denatured protein in a sample. `text(Each cooking method)` was repeated on numerous samples, and the average measurements are shown in the graph below.
problems/FL26HSB/media/34a.jpg
problems/FL26HSB/media/34b.jpg

B.Choice: Similar amounts of protein appear to be denatured in egg whites cooked on the stove for `text(120 seconds)` and for `text(150 seconds)`.

C.Choice: Less protein appears to be denatured in the egg whites cooked for `text(150 seconds)` than in those cooked for shorter durations of time.

D.Choice: More protein appears to be denatured in egg whites cooked in the microwave between `text(120 seconds)` and `text(150 seconds)` than in those cooked on the stove.

B.Choice: Each of the cells contains chloroplasts.

C.Choice: None of the cells contain mitochondria.

D.Choice: None of the cells contain a central vacuole.

Content: Between `1945` and `1952`, the brown tree snake was accidentally introduced to Guam, a small island in the Pacific Ocean. This snake population has increased rapidly since its introduction. With a growing number of these snakes on Guam, many native bird species have become extinct and other native organisms are threatened. Which of the following inferences can `bbtext(best)` be supported by these observations?

A.Choice: The number of nonnative predators may decrease when competition between predatory species is absent in an ecosystem.

B.Choice: Introducing a nonnative species to an isolated island may increase the biodiversity of natural predators found on that island.

C.Choice: Introducing a nonnative species into an ecosystem may cause a decrease in biodiversity of other species that are without natural predators.

D.Choice: The number of native predators may increase when nonnative species compete with natural predators for resources on an isolated island.

Content: Groups of students investigated the effect of detergents on algal growth. `text(Each group)` used the procedure listed below to compare detergents with and without phosphates.

:ibox:`1`. Label `text(two 1000-milliliter)` (`text(mL)`) beakers `1` and `2`, then add `text(500 mL )`of pond water that contains algae to `text(each beaker)`.

`2`. Use separate, clean pipettes to collect a `text(1 mL)` sample from `text(each beaker)`, then place `text(each sample)` on a separate slide.

`3`. Use a compound microscope to observe the algae, then shade in how much of the field of view has algal growth.

`4`. Add `10` drops of detergent containing phosphate to beaker `1`. Mix gently.

`5`. Add `10` drops of detergent that does not contain phosphate to beaker `2`. Mix gently.

`6`. Place both beakers near a sunny window.

`7`. `text(Each day)` for `text(5 days)`, collect a `text(1 mL)` sample from `text(each beaker)`, then shade in the field of view to indicate the estimated final algal growth.

`8`. Compare the results with those of other groups of students.
Which of the following describes the `bbtext(most)` significant flaw in this investigation?

A.Choice: In the investigation, the beakers were not kept near a sunny window for a long enough time period.

B.Choice: The investigation does not include a beaker that contains pond water without any detergent.

C.Choice: The investigation does not include a beaker that contains different types of algae.

D.Choice: In the investigation, the beakers were not maintained at the same temperature.

Content: In the African grass frog, the expression of multiple genes, including a gene called ASIP, is responsible for `text(three)` different spinal stripe phenotypes. The illustration below shows frogs with the `text(three)` observed phenotypes.
:ibox:`ultext(AFRICAN GRASS FROG SPINAL STRIPE PHENOTYPES)`

Scientists observed and counted frogs living on land surfaces and frogs living in trees. The scientists claim that the spinal stripe may be selected for when frogs live on land surfaces and selected against when frogs live in trees. How should this claim be evaluated?

A.Choice: Scientists should measure the spinal stripe width and calculate the average width for land-dwelling frogs and for tree-dwelling frogs.

B.Choice: Scientists should confirm that the frogs living on land surfaces and the frogs living in trees express the ASIP gene from the same chromosomal location.

C.Choice: Scientists should determine whether there is a difference in the frequency of expression of the ASIP gene between land-dwelling frogs and tree-dwelling frogs.

D.Choice: Scientists should compare species of frogs living on land surfaces and species of frogs living in trees to determine whether other populations have a spinal stripe.

Content: Genetic drift can result in fewer types of phenotypes among a species. Which of the following describes how genetic drift can result in this change?

Content: Some people have classified human earlobes as either being free or attached. `text(Two)` sets of researchers investigated the inheritance of earlobe type by categorizing a large number of offspring from many sets of parents. problems/FL26HSB/media/43b.jpg

Content: Some viruses enter the human body and attack the immune system. The immune system is then unable to remove these viruses, so they remain active in the body for a long time. Scientists have developed treatments using different types of medications to remove a particular virus from the body. The chart below describes the actions of `text(five)` types of these medications.
:table:problems/FL26HSB/supps/FL26HSB-T4.json
Which statement `bbtext(best)` explains why patients who carry this kind of virus are prescribed a long-term treatment of more than `text(one)` type of the listed medications?

A.Choice: Using more than `text(one)` type of these medications causes the virus to rearrange its genetic material before it is replicated.

B.Choice: Using more than `text(one)` type of these medications prevents the virus from copying its genetic material at a faster rate than normal.

C.Choice: Using more than `text(one)` type of these medications helps the virus enter the parts of the body that are resistant to `text(one)` type of medication.

D.Choice: Using more than `text(one)` type of these medications prevents the formation of versions of the virus that are resistant to any specific type of medication.
